quote: I've got a few questions to get started on your estimate. Is that cool?
stewart_read: Clean, low-friction consent transition into the verify section — schema-aligned framing that treats qualifying questions as routine rather than interrogation.
coaching_implication: This is a positive pattern worth reinforcing — the rep should keep using this framing on calls that don't DQ early, since it sets up verify without feeling like a checklist.

quote: Is there a space after that g or before that g?
stewart_read: Rep is burning time on granular address-formatting detail (space before/after 'G') that has no bearing on qualification, while the state-eligibility question — the actual gating fact — hasn't been asked yet.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as simple data-entry diligence rather than a sequencing failure, since accurate address capture matters for any booked appointment.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to front-load the state/region check before drilling into address spelling precision — confirm serviceability first, then perfect the address only if the lead survives that gate.

quote: We we actually we're not allowed to do Wisconsin.
stewart_read: This is the correct, necessary DQ — Ion doesn't service Wisconsin, so ending the call here is right procedure, not a rep error. Classified under protocol_violation only in the sense that the DQ check itself is a protocol; execution here is compliant, not violated.
alternative_hypothesis: None — this is a legitimate hard-gate DQ, not a missed opportunity.
coaching_implication: No action needed on the DQ decision itself; the only coaching angle is timing (see the space-after-G moment above) — get to this check faster.

stewart_read: Rep's apologetic sign-off frames the call itself as an imposition rather than a normal, professional outcome of a disqualification. Minor tone signal, not a substantive failure.
alternative_hypothesis: Could simply be a polite, low-stakes courtesy close with no real impact given the customer responds warmly regardless.
coaching_implication: Flag as a small demeanor note: on DQ calls, a neutral professional close ('Unfortunately we don't service that area yet, but I appreciate you filling out the form') maintains company posture better than an apology that implies the call itself was a bother.

quote: Where I'm at right now. Well, I already have solar panels on the roof.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers, unprompted, that their current residence already has solar — this is exactly the orphaned_flow trigger condition, surfaced after the DQ closed the call. The rep never engaged this thread.
alternative_hypothesis: The call was already functionally over (customer said 'have a great day' first) and the DQ'd address made this a dead lead regardless, so pursuing it may have yielded nothing.
coaching_implication: Even on a DQ'd address, a disclosed existing-solar situation at the customer's actual residence is worth a quick orphaned_flow question (own vs. lease, which company, system working) — costs 20 seconds and could surface a service or referral opportunity Ion can still act on.

quote: Hold on. Let me just fix this.
stewart_read: Rep openly narrates a data-entry correction mid-call rather than resolving it silently, adding to the sense of a mechanical, checklist-driven pace rather than a conversational one.
alternative_hypothesis: Transparency about fixing a typo can read as honest and low-stakes rather than unprofessional; the customer shows no irritation.
coaching_implication: Not a priority coaching item on its own, but pairs with the broader address-logistics slowdown — the fix is sequencing (state check first), not narration style.
